newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko claims crushing win in Belarus vote.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko claims crushing win in Belarus vote.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko claimed a crushing victory on Monday in a referendum widening his powers and said he would quickly reshape Belarus's political institutions.

Top electoral official Lidiya Yermoshina said 70.5 percent of the country's 7.2 million voters backed the president's constitutional draft while only 7.9 percent supported a draft written by his opponents.

The referendum, in which 84 percent of the electorate went to the polls, gives Lukashenko a green light to begin a major overhaul of the former Soviet republic's institutions and extend his own term in office by two years.
"Today we will set about forming the house of representatives," the president told a news conference. "There will be no need for new elections."
"There will be no annulment of the constitutional court, government and parliament," he said, making clear that the existing bodies would keep their functions for now.

Lukashenko said he would quickly form new lower and upper houses of parliament and decide the make-up of the constitutional court, which has overruled a string of his decrees. "I think they will be formed by Christmas although two months are set aside for this in the constitution," he said.
"I do not exclude that many members of the court will go into the new structure in the interests of continuity -- if they give up their political bias," he said.
Lukashenko, defying the existing constitution, the constitutional court, parliament and critics at home and abroad has declared the referendum would be legally binding, rather than just advisory.
Critics complained that the voting, which lasted for two weeks, was stacked with abuses and Lukashenko monopolised access to the media.
But it appeared unlikely that the existing parliament would be able to mount any effective resistance to Lukashenko's proposed changes.
